pages.text: Big snowflakes fell softly. A white blanket covered the yard.
"I want to make snow ducks that last and last!" Mumu packed snow firmly.
Two snow ducks were finished. Beaks in place, wings in place.
Dodo lifted one into her arms. "Keep snow ducks cozy so they don't freeze to death. I know! Beside the stove is perfect!"
On the shelf by the stove, the snow duck shrank and shrank. Its beak disappeared first.
Only a shiny puddle remained. Dodo blinked.
"My snow duck... must have gone swimming." Dodo peered at the puddle.
Mumu put the other one in the shade on the outside windowsill. A cold, windy spot.
The next morning, the snow duck was still there! Shiny, frozen solid.
They pressed their noses to the window. "Good morning, snow duck!" Dodo whispered, "Mine must be swimming in the stream by now." Two round white patches of breath appeared on the glass.
